title: B2 Level Check

questions.question: If I had studied harder, I ___ more confident now.
questions.explanation: A past condition can have a present result.

questions.question: Rarely ___ such a beautiful performance.
questions.explanation: Restrictive adverbs at the front can trigger inversion.

questions.question: She ___ have forgotten the meeting; she never misses one.
questions.explanation: Can't have + past participle expresses a strong negative deduction.

questions.question: I had my car ___ yesterday.
questions.explanation: Have + object + past participle describes a service arranged for someone.

questions.question: ___ the report, she sent it to the manager.
questions.explanation: Having + past participle shows the first action happened before the second.

questions.question: The suspect is believed ___ abroad.
questions.explanation: Is believed + to have + past participle reports an earlier action.

questions.question: The results ___ suggest that the policy was effective.
questions.explanation: Appear to is a cautious way to state a conclusion.

questions.question: The company needs to ___ a decision quickly.
questions.explanation: Make a decision is the standard collocation.

questions.question: Read: The road was closed after heavy rain, but engineers repaired the damaged bridge within two days. What happened first?
questions.explanation: The road closure happened before the engineers repaired the bridge.
answers: The rain stopped before the closure.

questions.question: Which is most appropriate in a formal report?
questions.explanation: Formal reports favor precise, neutral vocabulary.
